data.name: Vyshnavi
data.long_meaning: The name Vyshnavi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vishnu', meaning 'preserver of the universe'. The name Vyshnavi is a tribute to the God Vishnu and signifies one who dwells in His divine presence. This name is believed to bring protection, happiness, and prosperity.
data.spiritual_meaning: Vyshnavi is a name of the Goddess Lakshmi, who is the embodiment of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. It is also a name of Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe. This name is believed to connect the bearer with the divine energies of both Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Vishnu.
data.numerology_meaning: The name Vyshnavi is ruled by the number 6, which represents love, nurturing, and service to others. This number is associated with the 6th house in astrology, which governs health, harmony, and balance in relationships. The name Vyshnavi is believed to bring happiness and prosperity in personal and professional relationships.

data.spiritual_significance: The name Vyshnavi carries a profound spiritual significance as it signifies one who is in the divine presence of God Vishnu. It implies a deep spiritual connection with the deity and a constant endeavor to live one's life in accordance with his teachings. The name is believed to bring blessings of protection, happiness, and prosperity and helps the person uphold the virtues of faith, devotion, and self-control.

historical_references.reference: Vyshnavi was an epithet of Sri Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, prosperity and fortune in Hinduism. She is also known as Mahalakshmi and is the consort of Vishnu.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, circa 3rd millennium BCE - present
historical_references.context: Vyshnavi is a name used to signify the divine feminine associated with Vishnu, the preserver deity in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Vyshnavi is found in the Puranas, a set of eighteen Hindu scriptures. In one episode, the goddess Vyshnavi appears to grant a boon to King Mandhata, who had been cursed by the sage Durvasa. The goddess then grants the boon of immortality, under the condition that the king should never be called Mandhata again but instead be addressed as Vyshnava, or ‘protector of Vishnu’.
historical_references.context: In Hindu mythology, Vyshnavi is also a name given to those who are devoted to Vishnu and follow his teachings.
